fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response of one or more engines to a crew command
fha.effAc: Engine(s) deliver thrust different from that commanded; magnitude/direction of error determines whether a symmetric trajectory error or an asymmetric yaw results; on an outboard engine the asymmetry challenges directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the mismatch between commanded and actual thrust and correct trajectory/asymmetry; error may be masked until effects develop.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not bound the magnitude of the erroneous response, so the resulting effect (minor trajectory error vs asymmetry beyond control authority) cannot be established from the function definition. Classification requires the failure-effect study defining the error envelope. Left empty pending that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow thrust drift on one or more engines below the crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Slow thrust drift below the crew-detection threshold develops gradually; a symmetric drift produces a slow speed/trajectory deviation, an asymmetric drift a slowly building yaw/imbalance the crew does not act on.
fha.effCrew: By definition the crew continue normal duties and take no action; effect accumulates unnoticed until it crosses a detectable or consequential threshold.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level consequence of an unnoticed slow drift depends on the drift magnitude reachable before it becomes detectable/consequential and on whether it is symmetric or asymmetric — neither is bounded by the function definition. Cannot classify without the drift-rate/threshold analysis. Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground deceleration
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft effect: the SDD does not state the directional-control consequence of an asymmetric ground reverser deployment (reversers fitted to the two inboard engines only), nor the residual steering/braking authority available to counter it. Directional-control-on-ground effect required before classification.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft effect: reverse thrust is a ground deceleration aid on the two inboard engines only, with wheel braking as the primary stopper. The stopping consequence of reduced reverse depends on the braking margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared strip), which is not substantiated in the AFHA. Braking-margin effect required before classification.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft effect: total loss of reverse thrust leaves wheel braking as the deceleration means, and the stopping consequence turns on the braking margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface, from which the SDD says braking degradation is assessed). Without that overrun analysis the aircraft effect cannot be stated; do NOT default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of reverse thrust unannunciated at deceleration onset
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration relies on wheel braking alone with no reverse contribution; because the loss is unannunciated at onset the crew do not initiate compensating action (e.g. maximum manual braking) early, eroding the stopping margin on a semi-prepared strip where the 1,800 m requirement stands against ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation at deceleration onset; crew continue normal rollout technique and detect the shortfall only through deceleration cues, delaying compensating braking.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on stopping distance depends on the braking-degradation margin analysis (predicted ~1,080 m rollout vs 1,800 m requirement) which is not quantified in the provided material for the reverser-lost case; without that margin result the aircraft-level outcome (adequate stop vs overrun) cannot be derived, so severity is left for the engineer.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous attitude response to crew command
fha.effAc: The aircraft responds to a crew attitude command in pitch, roll or yaw differently from that intended, producing an unintended trajectory deviation the crew must recognise and counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive the mismatch between commanded and achieved attitude and must intervene to re-establish the intended flightpath.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The magnitude of the erroneous response and whether it is recoverable within the available envelope is not stated in the provided functional definition; the aircraft effect (transient upset vs loss of control) cannot be derived without that, so severity is left for the engineer.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded attitude motion with no command
fha.effAc: The aircraft develops an attitude change in pitch, roll or yaw with no corresponding crew command, producing an unintended trajectory deviation.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect uncommanded motion and must intervene to arrest the divergence and recover the intended attitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Rate and authority of the uncommanded motion, and whether the crew can arrest it within the envelope, are not derivable from the provided functional definition; aircraft effect (recoverable upset vs loss of control) is undetermined, so severity is left for the engineer. Note: this failure-condition id is not present in the current FCIM for SF-003.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow uncommanded attitude divergence below crew threshold
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded attitude divergence develops below the crew detection threshold; with the crew continuing their duties normally and taking no action, the divergence accumulates into a trajectory departure before it is recognised.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue normal duties, taking no compensating action while the divergence is below threshold; recognition and recovery occur only after the departure has grown.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The accumulated attitude/trajectory departure reached before crew detection is not derivable from the provided definition; the aircraft outcome (recoverable deviation vs unrecoverable departure) cannot be established, so severity is left for the engineer.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous attitude response below crew threshold
fha.effAc: The attitude response to crew commands is erroneous by an amount below the crew detection threshold; the crew act on the achieved response as if correct, producing a slowly accumulating trajectory error before recognition.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the response error and continue normal control inputs, taking no compensating action; the error is recognised only once it exceeds the detection threshold or manifests as a trajectory departure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The accumulated error and its trajectory consequence before detection are not derivable from the provided functional definition; aircraft effect is undetermined, so severity is left for the engineer. Note: this failure-condition id is not present in the current FCIM for SF-003.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment
fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift mismatch produces a rolling and yawing moment at low speed; a large asymmetry can exceed available lateral control authority near the ground.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter a lateral asymmetry at low speed and low altitude with increased workload; a large asymmetry may exceed roll authority.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on asymmetry magnitude and whether the resulting roll/yaw stays within available lateral control authority at low speed — not derivable from the aircraft-level function alone (the SDD notes asymmetry brakes at each section, but that is design mitigation, not a function-level effect). Missing: the controllability limit for asymmetric high-lift to determine whether the worst case is contained (Major/Hazardous) or exceeds authority near the ground (Catastrophic). Left empty pending that boundary.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move without a crew command, changing configuration and airspeed margin; the resulting pitch/lift change and, if asymmetric, roll may occur outside the intended envelope and at speeds beyond high-lift structural limits.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to an unexpected configuration change and trim/attitude excursion; workload rises depending on phase and speed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect ranges from a manageable trim change to a structural overspeed of the high-lift devices or a controllability event, depending on the speed at which the uncommanded movement occurs and whether it is symmetric — not resolvable from the aircraft-level function definition. Missing: the speed/phase envelope for uncommanded extension/retraction to bound the worst-case effect. Left empty rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric high-lift deployment below the detection/asymmetry-brake threshold
fha.effAc: Small uncommanded rolling moment from asymmetric flap/slat that is not annunciated and not arrested by the asymmetry brakes; crew fly a normal low-speed configuration with a persistent asymmetry the control system must trim out, reducing roll margin at low speed.
fha.effCrew: No alert; crew continue normal duties and are unaware, per the unaware assumption; asymmetry compensated by control inputs without diagnosis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The condition is bounded to be below the detection/asymmetry-brake threshold, but the SDD does not quantify that threshold or the residual rolling moment, so the actual controllability margin consumed at low speed cannot be established from the function/SDD alone. Cannot derive an aircraft effect severe enough to classify without the asymmetry threshold and roll-authority margin — needs engineering data (asymmetry brake set-point, roll authority at V_APP).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground-support / flotation configuration indication (status shown correct when it is not, or vice versa)
fha.effAc: Crew act on a false gear/ground-support configuration indication: a landing may be attempted or continued with the gear or flotation configuration not as indicated, or a valid configuration is rejected; on a semi-prepared surface an incorrect flotation/footprint state risks gear or surface failure during touchdown and rollout.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on the erroneous indication and take an inappropriate action (continue vs go-around / free-fall extension); mis-indication drives a wrong configuration decision at a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms dual independent downlock proximity sensing and gear-position indication but does not define what indication SF-005 (aircraft-level ground support/flotation status) presents, nor the consequence of acting on a false one; the aircraft outcome of a mis-indication (e.g. landing on an unlocked/incorrect gear on a semi-prepared strip) cannot be bounded from the function alone. Needs the indication definition and the touchdown consequence of an incorrect flotation/gear state — architecture/data gap.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ground support configuration integrity (loss of correct gear/flotation configuration not detected by the crew)
fha.effAc: Ground support / flotation configuration is not correctly established (e.g. a downlock or bogie not in the load-bearing state) and the loss is not detected; the crew continue normally and touch down / roll out on a semi-prepared surface with an unsound gear configuration, risking gear collapse, loss of footprint/flotation and departure from the prepared strip during the ~1,080 m rollout.
fha.effCrew: No indication of the degraded configuration; crew take no corrective action (unaware assumption) and land in the belief the gear/flotation is sound.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An undetected loss of ground-support configuration on a semi-prepared surface plausibly leads to gear collapse or runway departure, but the SDD does not establish which configuration elements are load-bearing at the aircraft level, the coverage of the sensing, or the touchdown/rollout consequence, so the aircraft effect and hence severity cannot be derived from the function alone. Needs the integrity-loss failure set and its landing consequence — architecture/data gap; do not default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The FCIM names 'partial loss of ground support capability' but neither the function definition ('Support the aircraft on the ground and provide flotation') nor the SDD specifies WHICH aspect degrades or the magnitude (e.g. loss of one bogie vs reduced strut capacity). Without a stated aircraft effect the class cannot be derived; scope the partial case (degraded footprint / partial gear collapse / single-bogie loss) before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced braking with degraded stopping performance
fha.effAc: Braking available but at reduced effectiveness; stopping distance increased. With ~720 m of margin between predicted rollout (~1,080 m) and the 1,800 m requirement on a semi-prepared surface, partial braking loss consumes margin and, at the limiting end, risks overrun; reverse thrust and aerodynamic drag partially compensate.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of degraded braking through increased pedal effort / reduced deceleration; may apply maximum braking and reverse thrust and adjust the stop.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated locked to the crew when not fully secured (erroneous lock status)
fha.effAc: The door is part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; a false 'locked' indication passes the take-off configuration check with the door not fully secured, permitting flight with a compromised pressure boundary and structural load path. Depending on pressurisation and airload, this can progress to loss of the door in flight with associated structural and decompression consequences.

fha.effAc: Restraint degradation occurring in flight is not annunciated; crew unaware. A subsequent shift of the 72.6 t blade can move CG outside limits and challenge controllability, with no indication to prompt action.

fha.fcDesc: Alert presented with incorrect priority
fha.effAc: An alert is presented but ordered incorrectly within the prioritised list, so a higher-criticality condition may be displaced below or masked by a lower-criticality one.
fha.effCrew: Crew may address a less-critical condition first or misjudge urgency; response to the more critical condition is delayed. Result depends on which conditions are mis-ranked.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Malfunction — the list is 'prioritised' (SDD §5.11.2) but the specific conditions and their relative criticality are not enumerated, so the aircraft effect of a mis-ranking cannot be bounded to a worst case. Cannot classify without the alert priority scheme. Engineer to classify per Table A6.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to present an alert for an existing condition
fha.effAc: A real system condition exists but no alert is raised for it; the aircraft continues with an unannunciated active fault.
fha.effCrew: Crew are unaware of the existing condition and continue normal duties, taking no action; a required procedure is not initiated. Outcome depends on the condition left unannunciated.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Malfunction with the crew unaware. The severity is set by the criticality of the specific condition that goes unannunciated (e.g. an unannunciated fire, pressurisation or restraint condition would drive high severity), which the SDD does not enumerate for the alerting function. Cannot ground a worst-case aircraft effect. Engineer to classify per Table A6.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression or omission of a required alert
fha.effAc: A required alert is suppressed or omitted and the omission itself is not detected, so the alerting function silently fails to present a condition with no fault indication.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no cue that an alert is missing and continue normal duties; both the underlying condition and the alerting failure remain unknown to the crew. Outcome depends on the suppressed condition.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Malfunction, crew unaware of both the condition and the alerting failure. Worst-case severity is driven by the criticality of the suppressed alert, which the SDD does not enumerate. Cannot ground an aircraft effect without the alert set and the self-monitoring coverage of the alerting function. Engineer to classify per Table A6.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: False fire, overheat or smoke warning with no actual event (erroneous detection)
fha.effAc: A warning is presented for a non-existent fire/overheat/smoke condition; aircraft remains fully airworthy but crew may respond to the false indication.
fha.effCrew: Crew must diagnose the alert against no corroborating cue and may execute a fire/overheat procedure (engine shutdown, extinguishant discharge, diversion) for a non-event; effect depends on the response, which the SDD does not specify.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft-level effect of a false fire warning turns on the assumed crew action (e.g. unnecessary engine shutdown or diversion) and its consequences, which the provided material does not state. Severity left empty pending the crew-response assumption.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection in one or more monitored zones
fha.effAc: Detection is lost in one or more zones (annunciated per the aware case); remaining zones stay monitored. A fire in the affected zone would go undetected, but the crew is aware the coverage is lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew is annunciated of the lost detection zone(s) and can apply operational limitations (e.g. dispatch decision, increased vigilance); no direct control of the fire risk beyond that.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect depends on which zone(s) lose detection and the crew/operational response to the annunciated loss (e.g. dispatch limitation vs continued flight), neither of which the provided material fixes. Severity left empty pending the affected-zone set and the operational credit taken.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage
fha.effAc: Overheat detection on the bleed-duct runs and main gear bays is lost; a bleed-duct leak/overheat or a gear-bay overheat (e.g. brake/tyre) would not be detected, risking damage to adjacent structure and systems in those zones before it is otherwise evident.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the overheat warning for these zones; detection of a bleed leak or gear-bay overheat then relies on secondary cues only.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the aircraft effect of an undetected bleed-duct or gear-bay overheat depends on the consequences of that overheat in those specific zones (structural/system damage, escalation), which the SDD describes as fitted coverage but does not characterise the resulting hazard. Left empty pending the overheat-consequence analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection in one or more monitored zones (partial loss of detection coverage)
fha.effAc: Aircraft loses timely detection in the affected zone(s); an initiating fire or overheat in a covered zone (engine nacelle, APU, bleed duct, gear bay or hold) develops without annunciation, delaying or preventing crew fire response. Effect on the aircraft depends on which zone is unmonitored and whether a fire actually initiates there.
fha.effCrew: Crew are not alerted to a fire/overheat in the affected zone and take no fire response; workload unchanged until an event manifests by other cues.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed except flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a single classification: the aircraft effect is conditional on an undetected fire actually initiating in the specific unmonitored zone, and the severity varies by zone (engine/APU fire zone vs hold smoke-only, no suppression). The function definition ("detect ... in monitored zones") does not by itself close the effect chain to a single worst-case outcome. Needs the per-zone fire-risk and the concurrent-fire exposure to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of a fire/overheat/smoke detection loop below warning threshold
fha.effAc: A detection loop is degraded but has not crossed the fault threshold, so no fault is annunciated; detection margin is silently reduced. Dual-loop AND/single-loop-degraded logic means the zone may still detect, or detection may be lost, without crew knowledge. Aircraft effect only manifests if a fire initiates while the degraded loop is relied upon.
fha.effCrew: No indication; crew continue duties normally and take no action (unaware condition).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed except flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the condition is a latent detection-margin reduction with no aircraft effect unless a fire concurrently initiates in the affected zone while the degraded loop is the active detection path. Severity therefore depends on the latent-plus-fire combination and the residual detection logic (dual-loop AND degrading to single loop), which the function definition alone does not resolve. Needs concurrent-fire exposure and residual-coverage analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced extinguishing capability in a protected zone
fha.effAc: Extinguishing available but at reduced capability in a protected zone; a fire may be partially controlled or require repeated/second-shot discharge that may be unavailable, extending the period the fire acts on nacelle structure, fuel and services before suppression.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute fire drill; may find suppression incomplete after discharge, requiring diversion with a possibly ongoing fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects stated, but 'reduced' capability is not dimensioned in the SDD (how much reduction, whether a second shot remains, which zone) so the residual ability to control a fire — and hence severity — cannot be derived; requires definition of the degraded extinguishing state.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of agent charge before demand
fha.effAc: Extinguishing agent unavailable at demand with no prior indication; on a subsequent fire the crew attempt discharge and find no suppression, equivalent to loss of extinguishing for that zone at the moment it is needed. No aircraft effect until a fire occurs.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the degraded state; on a fire they execute the drill expecting suppression and receive none, discovering the loss under emergency conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is a latent availability loss whose aircraft-level severity only manifests in combination with a subsequent fire; the FHA cannot fix severity for a condition whose outcome is a probabilistic combination of latency exposure and a second event — this belongs to the PSSA/quantitative assessment. Effects stated; severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of breathing oxygen supply to the flight crew (both cylinders / manifold), coincident with a demand event (decompression, smoke or fumes)
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable; requires immediate emergency descent to a survivable altitude. No structural or control effect from OXY loss itself.
fha.effCrew: With no breathing oxygen during a decompression or smoke/fume event at cruise, crew are exposed to hypoxia or incapacitating smoke/fumes during the descent; risk of impaired or incapacitated flight crew before reaching a breathable altitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point toward the severe end (potential crew incapacitation during a coincident emergency), but the classification is contingent on the coincident-event probability and on time-to-safe-altitude from FL260 versus useful-consciousness time — neither is given in the SDD. Left empty pending that operational/quantitative basis; do not read the blank as benign.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced breathing oxygen availability to the crew (e.g. single cylinder depleted / reduced reserve) during or before a demand event
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; reduced margin for the diversion duration the system must cover.
fha.effCrew: Crew oxygen available but at reduced reserve; either cylinder can supply the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve, so a demand event is survivable but with eroded margin for a prolonged diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states either cylinder alone can supply the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve, so the immediate demand case is covered — but whether the eroded margin still meets the diversion-time requirement at FL260 is not quantified. Cannot derive severity without the required-duration/reserve budget; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen supply to a single mask station (one regulator failed), other stations available
fha.effAc: No aircraft effect; other mask stations unaffected (regulators independent per mask).
fha.effCrew: One crew station without oxygen during a demand event; remaining crew stations supplied. With a nominal complement of two and provision for four, at least one pilot retains oxygen; affected crew member exposed to hypoxia/smoke unless able to relocate.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on whether the affected station is an on-duty pilot position and whether that pilot can be substituted — an operational/crew-complement judgement not fixed by the function definition (complement is two with provision for four). Left empty pending that operational basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of delivered oxygen quality (contaminated or off-specification breathing gas) delivered on demand
fha.effAc: No aircraft effect from OXY quality itself.
fha.effCrew: Crew breathe degraded/contaminated oxygen believing supply is good; potential for impaired performance or incapacitation depending on contaminant type and concentration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition (supply breathing oxygen on demand) does not characterise delivered-gas quality, contaminant type, concentration or physiological effect; the SDD indicates only cylinder pressure is monitored, with no quality monitoring stated. No basis to derive an aircraft/crew effect magnitude, so severity cannot be classified — left empty.. Engineer to classify.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a quality/contamination basis is supplied, SF-018-M3 could be classified rather than left empty.

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item.
